instruction: Select elements the way a user perceives them, using the project's accepted locator strategy
relevant_when: Test code or page objects define or use locators
context: Locator priority: role with accessible name, then label/placeholder/text, then the project's declared test-id attribute, then aria attributes, then ids, then class or structural CSS, then XPath. A project-wide test-id attribute declared in the profile or Playwright config is a first-class locator. Hashed CSS-module classes and XPath break on refactors and must be avoided.

checklist.name: no-class-selectors
checklist.rule: Locators do not depend on CSS class names, especially hashed or generated CSS-module classes; a role, label or test-id is used instead

checklist.name: role-first-for-interactive-elements
checklist.rule: Buttons, links, headings and form fields with a clear accessible name are located with getByRole or getByLabel unless the project's test-id is documented as the standard
checklist.relevant_when: A locator targets an interactive element

checklist.name: project-test-id-consistent
checklist.rule: When the project declares a test-id attribute, test-id locators use that attribute consistently rather than mixing several conventions
checklist.relevant_when: A locator uses a data-* attribute or getByTestId

checklist.name: positional-locators-justified
checklist.rule: Use the test, helper, and assertions to distinguish intentional ordering from position used as a substitute for identity. Surface only evidence-backed risks, as non-blocking suggestions; no adjacent comment is required.
checklist.relevant_when: A locator uses a positional selector

checklist.name: no-structural-selectors
checklist.rule: Locators do not rely on tag chains or DOM position (for example 'article h2 a' or a bare 'button'); a role or filter by text is used
